Loperamide oxide, another compound that interacts with PC10, further supports this pathway, as it is also a known microtubule-targeting agent. The presence of U251 as a downstream target of these interactions implies that the biological effects of vinblastine may be modulated by the activity of Loperamide oxide, which in turn influences U251. The scores indicate a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, suggesting that the observed interactions may be relevant in the context of drug-target interactions.
